description: Clipway test vectors, protocol v1 (see docs/PROTOCOL.md). Binary values are lowercase hex unless stated. Generated by tools/gen-vectors.mjs from relay/crypto.js.
derivation: P = HKDF-SHA256(S, empty salt, info clipway-proof, 16). id = hex(SHA-256(clipway-id || P))[0:32]. K_enc = HKDF-SHA256(S, empty salt, clipway-enc, 32). K_mac = HKDF-SHA256(S, empty salt, clipway-mac, 32).

envelope.note: AES-256-GCM, iv = nonce (12 bytes), aad = UTF-8 string, enc = standard base64 of ciphertext followed by the 16-byte tag. Same format as the Sonne encrypted state.

padding.note: The head plaintext is padded with spaces in a "pad" field, before the final brace, to the smallest multiple of 512 bytes that is at least its length + 9.

limits.note: The relay carries texts only: one envelope per item, at most the size of a 64 KiB text. Images and files (25 MiB at most) go directly (section 14).

text_item.note: Text copied on the Mac, inline. AAD of the head = chain id. The plaintext is the exact padded JSON string.

hello_item.note: hello: sent once after joining a chain and when the device name changes. No content fields.

offer_item.note: An image offered by the phone: the content stays on the phone, which listens on port 41234 at the addresses listed. The receiver connects there (section 14). name is optional for an image.

offer_file_item.note: A file of 150 000 bytes (byte i = i mod 251) offered by the Mac. The direct block below transfers it.

reply_item.note: The phone could not connect to any address of the Mac's offer: it says so through the relay.

refused_heads.note: Envelopes that open, but whose head must be refused (dropped and acknowledged): images and files never travel inside items any more, and nothing is cut in chunks.

negative.note: Both must be refused: authentication fails.

frames.note: Examples of relay frames (JSON text WebSocket frames). See docs/PROTOCOL.md, Relay.

error.message: this relay carries texts of 64 KB at most: images and files go directly between your devices

direct.note: Direct transfer of the file offered in offer_file_item. Records are length (4 bytes, big-endian) || nonce || ciphertext || tag; record nonces are fixed here, random in the apps.
direct.derivation: K_direct = HKDF-SHA256(S, empty salt, clipway-direct, 32). K_t = HKDF-SHA256(K_direct, empty salt, clipway-direct|<transfer>, 32). AAD of a record = clipway-direct|<transfer>|<get or put>|<index>.

negative.note: Each must be refused: get0 opened as put 0, get0 opened as get 1, get0 with another transfer's key, get0 with its last byte flipped.

private_hosts.note: Addresses a receiver may connect to (the local network): 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 169.254/16. Debug builds also allow loopback.

nearby.note: Nearby pairing over Bluetooth (docs/PROTOCOL.md, section 13). Keys are raw X25519 (RFC 7748, 32 bytes, little-endian u-coordinate). The fixed key pair is the one of RFC 7748, section 6.1: Mac = Alice, phone = Bob. The packets use the top-level S. Never use fixed keys or nonces outside tests.

der_prefixes.note: Wrap a raw key for APIs that take DER (java.security on Android, node:crypto). The raw public key is the last 32 bytes of the X.509 encoding.

nearby.derivation: commit = SHA-256(clipway-nearby-commit || pk_mac). T = pk_mac || pk_phone. Z = X25519. N = HKDF-SHA256(Z || T, empty salt, clipway-nearby, 32). K_sas = HKDF-SHA256(N, empty salt, clipway-nearby-sas, 32). K_key = HKDF-SHA256(N, empty salt, clipway-nearby-key, 32). sas = big-endian integer of HMAC-SHA256(K_sas, T)[0:6] mod 10000, 4 digits. confirm = HMAC-SHA256(K_sas, clipway-nearby-confirm || T)[0:16]. Packet = nonce || AES-256-GCM(K_key, aad, padded JSON) || tag.

leading_zero.note: Phone private key = SHA-256("clipway-nearby-vector-24"), the first of that series whose code starts with 0. Same Mac key.

low_order_keys.note: Z would be all zeros: refused (the library may throw instead).

high_bit_key.note: phone_public with the top bit of byte 31 set: refused before X25519.

own_key.note: A peer key equal to our own public key: refused.

wrong_commitment.note: The phone read commit, then a Mac key that does not match it: refused.

wrong_confirm.note: confirm with its last bit flipped: the Mac ends the attempt (Status 04).

tampered_packet.note: packet.bytes with its last bit flipped: authentication fails.

swapped_aad.note: The packet opened with the keys in the wrong order in the AAD: authentication fails.

short_packet.note: Any length other than 284 bytes: refused before decryption.

sessions.name: success, phone confirms first
sessions.note: The whole exchange. The packet read at the end is packet.bytes.

sessions.name: success, Mac confirms first, long read
sessions.note: Pair on the Mac first: the ready status goes out with the answer to the phone's confirmation. The packet is read in parts (ATT Read Blob): the Mac answers with the bytes from the offset; the radio cuts them to the MTU. The 120 s limit does not cut a ready session; it ends 10 s after the first read of the packet.

sessions.name: order, lengths and refused keys
sessions.note: Requests out of order are refused; a malformed or refused phone key does not use up the attempt.

sessions.name: one attempt per advertisement
sessions.note: Once a phone key is accepted, every other phone is refused and reads Status 05.

sessions.name: wrong confirmation
sessions.note: A wrong tag ends the attempt with Status 04; nothing can be read after.

sessions.name: canceled on the Mac
sessions.note: Cancel, closing the window or Show a code instead: Status 02.

sessions.name: expired
sessions.note: 120 s after the window opened, before both confirmations: Status 03.

sessions.name: phone left
sessions.note: The phone disconnects (Cancel on the phone, or out of range) before the end: no status, the attempt is over.
